integrity: The proof combines an exact exhaustive length-eight phase partition, an injective two-bit desubstitution to a four-letter fixed point, an injective four-letter desubstitution, and four explicit dyadic cyclic classes. A reproducible finite checker verifies the complete phase certificate, short cases, and higher regression cases, without substituting finite enumeration for the general proof.
scientific_limitations: The formula concerns the standard binary Rudin–Shapiro sequence, not generalized variants, and only the Lie invariant requiring every cyclic rotation. The length-eight phase recognizability is an implication of Allouche–Shallit (1993), Proposition 2, not a novel component of this result. A similar exact Lie spectrum may appear in an unindexed source.
title: Exact Lie complexity of the binary Rudin–Shapiro word
